skill.name: agent-checkpoint
skill.description: An undo button for AI agent work: save the project before a risky change, see exactly what changed, roll back in one command. Use when: Save a checkpoint before a refactor, codemod, dependency upgrade or migration; See exactly which files an agent added, changed or deleted; Roll back the whole project or a single file, and undo the roll back.
skill.summary: A public guide to saving, comparing, and restoring project checkpoints; the required implementation is not included.
skill.author: nexaiguy

content.user_title: Plan Recoverable Agent Changes with Checkpoints
content.value_statement: Agent changes can leave unwanted edits that are difficult to reverse. This guide explains checkpoint workflows for reviewing and restoring project files with a separately obtained implementation.
actual_capabilities: Documents checkpoint saving before refactors, dependency upgrades, codemods, and migrations.
Shows difference summaries and a patch inspection command.
Illustrates whole-project restoration, dry runs, and restoration of selected files.
Explains undoing a restore using an automatically saved checkpoint.
Describes Git and non-Git storage models and capture exclusions.
Outlines an optional Claude Code hook without supplying its implementation.
limitations: Only the public guide is included; scripts, extension source, templates, and hook implementation are absent.
Documented checkpoints remain on the project disk and do not replace independent backups.
The documented capture excludes ignored files, nested repositories, submodules, and files above the default 50 MB limit.
The documented runtime needs Python 3.8+; exact line endings need Git 2.40+, and Windows symlinks need Developer Mode or administrator rights.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the documented checkpoint workflow and identify what this guide-only package cannot execute.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a checkpoint plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan checkpoints for my dependency upgrade. Include capture exclusions, backup requirements, and a check that the separate implementation is installed.

prompt_templates.title: Plan selective recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Using my supplied difference summary, identify unintended deletions and propose a selective restore dry run. Request approval before changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Recovering selected files after reviewing changes

prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate the documented Claude Code hook for our workflow. Separate documented claims from verified behavior and list missing implementation evidence.

output_examples.input: Can this package save a checkpoint before my refactor?
output_examples.output: This package contains only a guide. Obtain and review the separate implementation before saving checkpoints; no checkpoint has been created.

output_examples.input: Plan recovery for two unintended file deletions without discarding the remaining refactor.
output: Confirm the required files exist in the selected checkpoint.
Preview restoration limited to those two files.
Review the preview and approve the restore before execution.
After execution, verify both files and record the documented undo checkpoint.

output_examples.input: Will checkpoints protect every project file from disk failure?
output_examples.output: No. The guide describes same-disk checkpoints with capture exclusions. Use an independent backup for disk failure and verify which files are protected.

best_practices: Obtain and audit the separate implementation before relying on checkpoint creation or restore guarantees.
Review capture exclusions and maintain independent backups for important project data.
Inspect differences and preview restores before approving changes to project files.
anti_patterns: Treating this guide-only package as an installed checkpoint utility.
Assuming same-disk checkpoints replace backups or include ignored secrets.
Restoring an entire project without reviewing the target checkpoint and affected files.

faq.question: Does this package include the checkpoint utility?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly excludes scripts, extension source, and templates from the original package.

faq.question: Can I use the documented workflow with Claude or Codex?
faq.answer: The guide targets agents that can run Python 3.8+, including Claude Code and Codex. The separate implementation is required.

faq.question: Does the guide include an automatic Claude Code hook?
faq.answer: It describes a hook before modifying Bash commands and subagent starts, but does not include the hook implementation.

faq.question: Do checkpoints change my Git branch?
faq.answer: The guide says checkpoints use separate Git references and a private index. The missing implementation prevents independent verification of this behavior.

faq.question: Are environment files protected?
faq.answer: The guide says ignored files are excluded. Verify ignore rules and implementation behavior; do not assume every environment file is ignored.

faq.question: Can a restore be reversed?
faq.answer: The guide says each restore first saves the current state. Verify this behavior with the separate implementation before relying on recovery.
